analysis.title: US CPI: October preview
key_insights: CACIB expects October headline CPI at +0.29% MoM SA and core at +0.26% MoM SA. Bloomberg average consensus for core is 0.24% MoM SA, so CACIB is 2bp above.

No YoY figure can be given for October because the BLS never published the October 2025 index (government shutdown). Using an arbitrary 325.604 index level for October 2025, the US fixings market marks October 2026 headline at 3.56% YoY, and CACIB is 2bp above that.

Core is expected back near 0.25% MoM SA, softer than August (0.29%, boosted by noise in telephone services) and September (0.33%). The 3M annualised core rate would be 3.53% in October, the highest since January 2025.

Energy inputs come from gasoline and natural gas futures. After the recent sharp drop in Brent, the model puts headline CPI at about 3.5-3.6% YoY until February 2027. Headline peaked at 4.25% YoY in May 2026.

Limited second-round effects from higher energy prices (Iran war) are visible in core, except airfares. Some pass-through is starting in core goods but nothing significant yet. No major CPI impact is expected from the midterm election result beyond lower crude already in the model.
Core CPI is forecast at 2.8-2.9% YoY until February 2027, then easing toward 2.5% by end-2027, versus an average 2.6% YoY so far in 2026.

Base effects dominate core YoY for six months. Last year's tariffs leave the YoY calculation (lowering core goods), while OER and rent YoY will be abnormally strong from November 2026 to March 2027 because of BLS methodology choices after the 2025 shutdown.

Services are forecast at +0.25% MoM SA, with airfares +1.48% and OER +0.31% on the strong side, and hotels -1.33% and internet services -0.8% on the weak side. Telephone services is forecast at +0.3%.

Core goods are forecast at +0.25% MoM SA, with education and communication commodities +0.4% (chipset and memory prices) and recreation commodities +0.51% (higher input costs). Core goods are expected to stay near 1% YoY until about mid-Q2 2027 and fall to about 0.4% YoY by end-2027.

Food is forecast at +0.34% MoM SA, with cereals and bakery +0.70% and meats, poultry, fish and eggs +0.07%. Food CPI is expected to stay near 3% YoY and run around 3.5% into Q4 2027 and Q1 2028, with El Nino an upside risk.

Energy is forecast at +0.57% MoM SA (-0.63% NSA): motor fuel -0.75% NSA, electricity -0.9%, natural gas +0.6%. Energy YoY peaked at 23.5% in May 2026 and was 20.5% in September. It is expected at 17-20% YoY until February 2027, then back near 0% as the March and April 2025 moves leave the sample.

PCE: the October PPI on 13 November will be used to finalise PCE forecasts. A late-September methodology change removed portfolio management and investment advice from the relevant PCE components. That component was revised to 8.6% YoY in July from 20.8%, cutting more than 0.2ppt from YoY core PCE.
Core PCE is still 3.1% YoY, more than a full point above target. The October CPI would improve on September but remain firmer than ideal for the Fed.

Fed view: CACIB expects a 25bp hike in December and a final 25bp hike in March, totalling 75bp to reverse last year's insurance cuts, before another pause. The Fed held in October, helped by the PCE revisions. Recent Fedspeak supports gradual tightening.

risk_factors: No October 2025 CPI index exists because of the government shutdown, so YoY comparisons and market consensus for YoY are unavailable.
BLS methodology choices after the 2025 shutdown will make OER and rent YoY abnormally strong from November 2026 to March 2027.
Core goods face higher imported and logistics costs from the energy crisis, keeping core goods near 1% YoY until about mid-Q2 2027.
El Nino is an upside risk to food CPI.
Fertiliser and fuel prices are rising and are expected to pass through slowly to food CPI.
Core PCE at 3.1% YoY and firm CPI could support further Fed tightening.
Lower immigration (potentially inflationary via labour) and AI (potentially deflationary medium term) are conflicting narratives that CACIB says do not dominate the one-year outlook.
vol_and_positioning: The US CPI fixings market marks October 2026 headline YoY at 3.56%, using an arbitrary 325.604 level for the October 2025 index. CACIB is 2bp above the market.
geopolitical: Iran war has raised energy prices, with limited second-round effects in core CPI so far, mainly airfares.
The blue wave result in the midterm elections is not expected to have a major CPI impact beyond lower crude oil prices.
